flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How do bacteria reproduce when they are cultured?
flashcard_questions.a: By binary fission, splitting into two identical daughter cells.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How often can bacteria divide under ideal conditions?
(Higher) How is an inoculating loop sterilised before use?
flashcard_questions.a: By passing it through a Bunsen flame until it glows red.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why must a sterilised inoculating loop cool in the air?
flashcard_questions.a: Touching a surface would pick up contaminants.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why is the Petri dish lid only lifted slightly when inoculating?
flashcard_questions.a: To minimise exposure to airborne microorganisms.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why is a Petri dish taped rather than sealed all the way round?
flashcard_questions.a: To let air in and stop anaerobic pathogens growing.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why is an incubated agar plate stored upside down?
flashcard_questions.a: To stop condensation dripping onto the colonies.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why are school agar plates incubated at a maximum of 25 °C?
flashcard_questions.a: Higher temperatures could encourage harmful human pathogens to grow.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What does a zone of inhibition on an agar plate show?
flashcard_questions.a: Where the substance has killed or prevented bacterial growth.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What does a larger zone of inhibition tell you?
flashcard_questions.a: That antibiotic or disinfectant is more effective against that bacterium.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What is the control disc soaked in for the antibiotic practical?
(Higher) How do aphids damage the plant they feed on?
flashcard_questions.a: They suck sap from the phloem, removing sugars and amino acids.

flashcard_questions.q: Which mineral ion deficiency causes stunted growth in a plant?
Why does magnesium deficiency turn a plant's leaves yellow?
flashcard_questions.a: Magnesium is needed to make chlorophyll.

flashcard_questions.q: Which mechanical defence do roses and cacti use against animals?

notes: 15 cards: the culturing, aseptic technique, zone of inhibition and plant-disease-detection content sits inside the lesson's higher-only block, so those 12 cards are prefixed '(Higher)'. Mix is 6 practical-technique 'why' cards, 2 practical-to-result cards (zone meaning, zone size), 1 practical control card, 1 process card (binary fission), 1 value card (20 minutes), 1 pest mechanism, plus 3 non-tiered cards from the ion deficiency and plant defence sections. Dropped the plant defence and detection method lists as enumerations, and the πr² worked example as calculation practice.
